nodes.summary: Cut a bang proposition by commuting through its supplying proof to an axiom or promotion. At promotion, delegates to `questMulticut` with one selected occurrence.
nodes.title: Cut admissibility for a bang proposition

nodes.summary: The core cut admissibility implementation: given decidable atom equality and explicit list sequents, combine cut-free proofs of dual distinguished propositions into a cut-free proof of the sum of their residual sequents. Recurses on proposition size.
nodes.title: Core cut admissibility procedure on list sequents

nodes.summary: Cut admissibility for non-exponential propositions: uses height induction on the sum of premise heights, with commuting cases for non-principal rules. Only callable when neither `a` nor `a⫠` is a question mark.
nodes.title: Cut admissibility for non-exponential propositions

nodes.summary: The proposition-size induction step for cut admissibility. Dispatches to `bangCutAdm`, `questCutAdm`, or `cutAdmNonExponential` depending on the top-level connective.
nodes.title: Proposition-size induction step for cut admissibility

nodes.summary: Public entry point for cut admissibility: given cut-free proofs of `a ::ₘ Γ` and `a⫠ ::ₘ Δ`, produce a cut-free proof of `(Γ : Sequent) + Δ`.
nodes.title: Cut admissibility for cut-free classical linear logic proofs

nodes.summary: Compute cut-free proofs by structural recursion on the original (possibly non-cut-free) proof. Each case recursively normalises the premises, then uses `cutAdm` at each cut. The list `Γ` is the explicit sequent for the current subgoal.
nodes.title: Cut elimination by structural recursion on the proof

nodes.summary: List-based cut elimination with the concrete list presentation explicit.
nodes.title: List-based cut elimination in the source calculus

nodes.summary: Cut elimination, using a noncomputable list presentation.
nodes.title: Cut elimination with a noncomputable list presentation

nodes.summary: Reduce a pair of principal rules whose conclusions match the cut proposition. Every recursive call is on a proper subproposition of the original cut proposition, so termination is guaranteed by proposition size.
nodes.title: Reduction of a cut between matching principal rules

nodes.summary: The shape of a cut-free proof when the cut proposition is in principal position. Each constructor corresponds to a rule whose conclusion matches the cut proposition. Axioms are handled separately in `cutStep`. Tensor carries explicit presentations of both premises' residual contexts.
nodes.title: Principal shapes of a cut-free proof at the cut proposition

nodes.summary: Decompose a cut against a cut-free proof: either expose a principal rule matching the cut proposition, or commute the cut through one inference (non-principal case). Every recursive call is on a strictly shorter supplying derivation.
nodes.title: Cut step exposing a principal rule or commuting the cut

nodes.summary: Present both summands using only the supplied list.
nodes.title: List presentations of two summands from a supplied list

nodes.summary: Present a tail without choosing a multiset representative.
nodes.title: List presentation of a tail without choosing a representative

nodes.summary: Reverse the exponential cut orientation using `bangCutAdm`, duality, and exchange. This is a wrapper, not a recursive call that swaps premises at the same measure.
nodes.title: Question-mark cut via the bang case, duality and exchange

nodes.summary: Split a selected occurrence against a rule head; the rule tail can be a multiset.
nodes.title: Splitting a selected occurrence against a rule head

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
